outcome: Help clinicians and coders create complete, evidence-linked drafts faster while preserving professional sign-off; benefits include less administrative time, better completeness, and traceable…
overview: Clinicians and coders spend hours re-entering encounter evidence that already exists, driving burnout, delayed records and revenue leakage. This solution captures approved encounter sources — ambient conversation, dictation and structured EHR data — and drafts complete, evidence-linked clinical notes and candidate codes, flagging missing support rather than inventing it. Every draft is reviewed, edited and signed off by the responsible clinician or coder before it reaches the record, with a full edit history retained. A controlled specialty pilot of 8–12 weeks targets a 25% reduction in documentation and coding time, better agreed completeness measures and fewer avoidable queries, with professional accountability preserved throughout.

benefits.text: Reduce clinician documentation and coder processing time by a target 25%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate against the customer’s own EHR-timestamp baseline in a controlled specialty pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Improve note completeness and reduce avoidable coding queries and downstream rework
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on specialty vocabulary calibration and the quality of encounter capture; measured against agreed completeness and query baselines

benefits.text: Retain 100% clinician and coder sign-off with a traceable edit history on every record
benefits.source: Reference architecture review workflow, Redington Healthcare catalogue,
benefits.limits: A design property of the mandatory-review workflow, verified in UAT; not a claim about draft accuracy

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); encounter audio and clinical text stay in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, in line with UAE and Saudi health-data regulations

notFor.situation: No approved coding policy or note standards to draft against
notFor.why: Drafting quality is measured against the customer’s own standards; without them there is no honest completeness measure and no acceptance basis

notFor.situation: Expectation of autonomous documentation or coding without professional sign-off
notFor.why: Drafts are decision support for accountable professionals; the workflow requires clinician and coder approval by design, and the source catalogue makes no autonomous claim

notFor.situation: Specialties where consent for ambient capture cannot be operationalised
notFor.why: Ambient documentation depends on lawful, consented audio capture in the consultation room

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns note standards, coding policy and professional accountability · Duration: 8–12-week pilot; 16–28 weeks to production rollout
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, clinical-NLP engineer, integration engineer; customer CMIO or clinical lead, HIM/coding lead, EHR integration lead, privacy and security approvers · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Specialty discovery and baseline agreement
2) Template, vocabulary and coding-policy calibration
3) EHR and revenue-cycle integration
4) Clinical safety, privacy and security testing
5) Controlled pilot with weekly quality review
6) Stabilisation, benefit review and handover
